name: Sikafloor CureHard-24
paste:
SIKAFLOOR® CUREHARD-24: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikafloor® CureHard-24, April 2023, Version 02.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/sikafloor_curehard-24.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikafloor® CureHard-24 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.01).
1.2 Product description. Sikafloor® CureHard-24 is a one part, clear sodium silicate based liquid to harden and provide an impregnating seal fresh or hardened concrete.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikafloor® CureHard-24 may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Horizontal old or new concrete surfaces, where a hard surface with light to moderate abrasion resistance is required e.g. warehouses, industrial plants, stores, shopping malls, parking structures, service stations, hangars etc.
    - as an impreganting sealer on concrete slabs where no specific curing efficiency or standards are required
    - Suitable for interior or exterior applications as an impregating sealer.
    - As a desifier in the process of grinding and polishing concrete.
    - Dust-proofing of prefabricated concrete elements.
    - Suitable for protection against ingress (Principle 1, method 1.2 of EN 1504-9)
    - Suitable for physical resistance (Principle 5, method 5.2 of EN 1504-9)
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikafloor® CureHard-24
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Sodium silicate / water based based transparent surface hardener, dust proofer, densifier and impregnating sealer for concrete
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates. Impregnation for surface protection of concrete according to EN 1504-2:2004, ingress protection and physical resistance, Declaration of Performance 02 08 03 04 004 0 000001 1180, certified by notified factory production control certification body 1020, certificate of conformity of the factory production control 020025682, and provided with the CE marking.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-9: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Uses (p.1).
    - EN 1504-2:2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1766: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Technical Information > Abrasion resistance (p.2); Technical Information > Penetration depth (p.2); Technical Information > Resistance to impact (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 6272-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Resistance to impact (p.2).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1504-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Penetration depth (p.2).
    - EN 1062-3: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Water absorption (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Ready to use
    - Easy to apply
    - Improved chemical and abrasion resistance compared to untreated concrete
    - Reduced dusting of concrete floors
    - Very low VOC
    - Non-yellowing
    - Good penetration - designed to pentrate, not provide a surface seal
    - Solvent free
    - Colourless and odourless
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Sodium silicate water dilution
    - Appearance and colour: Clear liquid
    - Density: ~1.2 kg/l (at +20 °C)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Solid content by mass: ~24 %
    - Abrasion resistance: 50 mg or 81.5 % increase in abrasion resistance compared to untreated sample; (C(0,70) concrete according to EN 1766) (Taber Abraser, H-22; Wheel, 1000 g / 1000 cycles) (EN 5740-1)
    - Resistance to impact: 60 Nm (class III: ≥ 20 Nm); Sample (MC(0,40) concrete according to EN 1766 (EN 6272-1)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: 4.8 N/mm²; Sample (MC(0,70) concrete according to EN 1766 (EN 1542)
    - Penetration depth: 5.5 mm; Sample (MC(0,70) concrete according to EN 1766 (EN 1504-2)
    - Water absorption: w = 0.03 kg/m²×h0.5; (on a substrate w > 1 kg/m² h0.5) (EN 1062-3)
2.7 System structure. General sealer: 1–2 coats Hardener / Sealer: 1–2 coats
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 5L,20 L poly cube - 200 L drum
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protect from frost.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - Hardened / old concrete
    - Surfaces must be sound, open textured, clean, free from frost, laitance, surface water, oils, grease, coatings, all loosely adhering particles and other surface contaminants.
    - If in doubt apply a test area first.
    - Note that Sikafloor® CureHard-24 used a a general sealer will not penetrate burnished or fully polished concrete and is not suitable for this appliction.
    - For best results with new concrete floors wait for 7–14 days after placement or until after cement has sufficiently hydrated prior to treatment with Sikafloor® CureHard-24.
3.3 Substrate preparation.
    - Hardened / old concrete
    - The substrate must be prepared by suitable cleaning method such as high pressure water cleaning or by ride-on cleaning machines. Allow drying prior to application. All dust, dirt, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by brush and / or vacuum.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Drying time: The surface is touch-dry after 2 hours at +20 °C. Maximum sealing and hardening effect achieved after ~7 days at +20 °C.
4.3 Consumption. Approx 0.15–0.25 l/m²/coat (4–7 m²/l/coat). as a densifier Approx 8- 10m2 as a general sealer/imprenator; This figure is theoretical and does not include for any additional material required due to surface porosity, surface profile, variations in level and wastage etc.
4.4 Waiting time to overcoating. Where 2 coats are required, to ensure maximum densification, the second coat can be installed 2–4 hours following the first. Allow previous coats to become tack free before applying additional coats.
    | Temperature | Time |
    | +5 °C | ~ 3.5 hours |
    | +10 °C | ~ 3 hours |
    | +20 °C | ~ 2 hours |
    | +25 °C | ~ 1.5 hours |
    | Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions particularly temperature and relative humidity |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.5 Applied product ready for use.
    | Substrate temperature | Fully serviceable |
    | +10°C | ~ 6 hours |
    | +20°C | ~ 5 hours |
    | +30°C | ~ 4 hours |
    Note printed: Note: Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient and substrate conditions.
4.6 Application.
    - Hardened Concrete Full hardening - densifying process
    - Apply in a continuous film using a high volume low pressure spray unit.
    - To ensure maximum penetration, scrub material into the surface with a soft bristle broom or floor-scrubbing machine (min. 30 minutes), until the material begins to gel and becomes slippery. Wet the material slightly with a water spray and rework it into the surface for another 10 to 20 minutes. After this process, rinse the floor and remove any excess material using a squeegee, wet vacuum or mop.
    - On porous, rough-textured or broom-finished surfaces, a second coat may be required.
    - For large surfaces and higher placing rates, mechanical equipment such as ride-on cleaning machines can be also used to place, brush in and remove the excess material from the surface.
    - Thanks to proceeding chemical reaction the rate of water-tightness increases gradually, whereas maximum sealing and hardening effect occurs earliest after 7 days. Gloss of the surface gradually increases during 30 to 90 days depending upon cleaning frequency.
    - As a densifier in grind/polish system
    - Apply Product by spray or squeegee to the surface at the 80 grit stage of grinding. Two applications are recommended. If product is applied at the polishing stage uneven colour may result. Do not use Sikafloor® CureHard-24 as a final sealer on polished, finished floors as a sealer - it will not penetrate and will result in an unsatisfactory outcome that will have to be stripped off.
    - As a general sealer
    - Apply with manual spray equipment or roller at a rate of approx 8-10m2 per litre depending on the porosity of the substrate. Apply evenly without any excess product or pooling on the surface. Two coats recommended. Do not allow excess product to remain on the surface - whitening or stickiness of the excess product may occur and leave discolouration. Do not apply as a general sealer on fully burnished/closed/dense concrete surfaces as it will be unable to pentrate.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment.
    - Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use.
    - Hardened / cured material can only be mechanically removed.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not use sprayers which have previously been used for spraying silicones or release agents (oils).
    - In hot weather (above +25 °C) store Sikafloor® CureHard-24 in a cool place prior to use.
    - At low temperatures (below +10 °C) the product may thicken and be difficult to spray.
    - Do not mix different formulations of Sika® or other curing membranes.
    - Ensure spraying equipment is cleaned thoroughly prior to use and any residues of previous membranes are removed.
    - Sikafloor® CureHard-24 must be treated mechanically (from light to heavy shot blasting depending on the depth of the penetration) prior to the application of a coating system.
    - Immediately wash over-spray from glass, aluminium or highly polished surfaces with water to avoid etching of surfaces.
    - Do not use on substrates treated previously with curing agents, membrane forming sealers or asphalt until these layers have been removed completely.
    - Gelification time may be increased at low temperatures (below +10 °C), high humidity (from 80 % to 100 %) or wind free conditions.
    - In hot weather conditions (above +25 °C), gelling may occur before material has penetrated sufficiently. In such case, apply additional Sikafloor® CureHard-24 to keep the surface wet for the recommended 30 minutes.
    - When applying, leave no dry spots in order to have homogenous performance. Touch up where necessary.
    - For both old and new concrete, thoroughly wash and remove residue or excess material. This is important as it is difficult to do so if allowed to dry and may result in unsightly white stains or stckiness and discolouration . This residue solution is non-toxic and can be emptied into a sanitary sewer.
    - As a general sealer,Sikafloor® CureHard-24 application is designed to fully penetrate and impregnate - ensure no excess product remains on the surface post application - A trial area is recommended to ensure ability to penetrate the concrete surface.
    - Performance enhancement of the substrates will vary greatly depending on the age, cement content, humidity content, porosity and penetration of the product into the substrate.
    - Sikafloor® CureHard-24 will not compensate for poor substrates with low cement content. It is not intended for substrates which are lightweight or extremely porous or have worn (aggregate exposed) surfaces.
    - Sikafloor® CureHard-24 will not hide serious staining or excessive wear.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. 100 % max.
5.4 Substrate temperature. +5 °C min. / +35°C max.
5.5 Substrate moisture content. Can be applied on a surface dry substrate.
5.6 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - In hot weather (above +25 °C) store Sikafloor® CureHard-24 in a cool place prior to use.
    - At low temperatures (below +10 °C) the product may thicken and be difficult to spray.
    - Gelification time may be increased at low temperatures (below +10 °C), high humidity (from 80 % to 100 %) or wind free conditions.
    - In hot weather conditions (above +25 °C), gelling may occur before material has penetrated sufficiently. In such case, apply additional Sikafloor® CureHard-24 to keep the surface wet for the recommended 30 minutes.
    - Performance enhancement of the substrates will vary greatly depending on the age, cement content, humidity content, porosity and penetration of the product into the substrate.
5.7 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - As a general sealer,Sikafloor® CureHard-24 application is designed to fully penetrate and impregnate - ensure no excess product remains on the surface post application - A trial area is recommended to ensure ability to penetrate the concrete surface.
    - If in doubt apply a test area first.
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Abrasion resistance: 50 mg or 81.5 % increase in abrasion resistance compared to untreated sample; (C(0,70) concrete according to EN 1766) (Taber Abraser, H-22; Wheel, 1000 g / 1000 cycles) (EN 5740-1)
    - Resistance to impact: 60 Nm (class III: ≥ 20 Nm); Sample (MC(0,40) concrete according to EN 1766 (EN 6272-1)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: 4.8 N/mm²; Sample (MC(0,70) concrete according to EN 1766 (EN 1542)
    - Penetration depth: 5.5 mm; Sample (MC(0,70) concrete according to EN 1766 (EN 1504-2)
    - Water absorption: w = 0.03 kg/m²×h0.5; (on a substrate w > 1 kg/m² h0.5) (EN 1062-3)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikafloor® CureHard-24, April 2023, Version 02.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/sikafloor_curehard-24.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikafloor CureHard 24, version 12/09/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/8/MSDS%20Sikafloor%C2%AE%20CureHard-24%20GHS7.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Maintenance. To maintain the appearance of the floor after application, Sikafloor® CureHard-24 must have all spillages removed immediately and must be regularly cleaned using rotary brushes, mechanical scrubbers, scrubber dryers, high pressure washers, wash and vacuum techniques, etc., using suitable detergents and waxes. The frequency and intensity of the wet cleaning will directly influence the how soon and how deep the glossy anti-dust surface develops.
6.4 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.5 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.6 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
